project1.title: COTS : Take Your Destiny Into Your Own Wings
project1.subtitle: PC and Mobile Roguelike tower defense game
project1.description: A roguelike tower defense game made with Unity. This game was designed to be both mobile and PC compatible. This project is being made in a team of 7, with 4 artists and 3 developers, it is undoubtedly my largest project. Being a small team, I’ve had to work on various different tasks such as gameplay development, bug fixing, refactoring, code cleaning, UI/UX, game design, marketing and communications. COTS is not yet released, with an expected release January 2026, so no git or playable version is available today.

project2.title: Fast, orientable, aperiodic ocean
project2.subtitle: synthesis using tiling and blending in Godot
project2.description: A study and research project for the first year of my masters degree in a group of four. This project was an implementation of the work by N. Lutz et Al. [2019] describing the generation of oceans with shaders using tiling and blending.(view “Implemented Paper” button for the source). Our work consisted of understanding and implementing this work into Godot, more specifically with GdShader and GLSL. Our work includes ocean generation using tinear tiling and Blending, orientable oceans with flow maps, LEAN mapping (specular light dampening, not perfectly implemented), and many different debug tools made in Godot to help complete the project.

project3.title: Fisheye Engine
project3.subtitle: Game engine "from scratch" in C++
project3.description: Three-month university project done in pairs with the objective of creating a game engine based on openGL. Our project implements, among other things, deferred rendering, an almost complete physics engine and a user interaction system. Particular attention has been paid to the game developer experience, with an intuitive and secure code architecture using the expressive power of modern C++.

project4.title: MAIge Academy
project4.subtitle: Advanced multi-agent system with strategies in Godot
project4.description: A month long four person university project made for a multi agent systems course using Godot. This project implements relatively advanced agents (student and teacher) with each boasting several strategies and responses. The teacher has multiple spells that are used in different conditions (ie number of students, range, etc..) and the students have multiple different strategies to escape the teacher that can be chosen in the game’s menu (ie go as far from the teacher as possible, go for the closest candy always, go alone, go in pairs…). There are no player controls, and it is available to play on Itch.

project5.title: AIgricultor
project5.subtitle: Simple multi agent system in Godot
project5.description: A month long university project made for a multi agent systems course. This project implements two simple agents (dog and sheep) that react to changes in the environment, in our case, the dog will react to any sheep escaping the enclosure and push them back in, and the sheep will try to escape when the dog isn’t around. This project was made in a group of 4 using the Godot engine. There are no player controls, and it is available to play on Itch.

project6.title: HarMONEY
project6.subtitle: Automatic or manual color harmonisation software
project6.description:
A research project for an image processing course that consisted of making a state of the art on the subject of color harmonization, and implementing different algorithms described in scientific papers. Color harmonization means to choose an image, a harmonic template (on the color wheel), and then  to move all the colors to reach the closest color in that harmony. It was a 3-person project, done in Python and mainly using the OpenCV library for image treatment. 
 (The video is a comedic presentation of the project and it is in french.)

project7.title: Raytracer
project7.subtitle: Basic Raytracer made in C++
project7.description: A basic OpenGL C++ Raytracer made for a 3D programming course. My project includes compatibility with simple shapes like cubes and spheres, and can compute triangle intersections, which, using a KD-Tree structure to accelerate, allowing compatibility with more advanced meshes. This project also includes a simple Phong Shader, simulates reflection (ie mirrors), refraction (ie glass), soft shadows (or hard shadows for faster computation), and a basic motion blur effect for spheres.

project8.title: Nokia Jam 6 : The Adventures of Trognon
project8.subtitle: 2D Platformer
project8.description: This was my first ever game jam, as well as my first real experience with Godot and game engines in general. The work was done in pairs and lasted only a day and a half, it is a simple platformer with the constraint of being able to run on an old Nokia phone (limited colors, resolution, sounds, etc…). The player must collect keys to open doors, and loses if they move when the timer hits FREEZE!, or when in contact with spikes or cannon balls. The game is available to play on Itch.

project9.title: Imagine Jam 2025 : CrashLands
project9.subtitle: Short 2D RPG
project9.description: A 1.5 day game jam project done in Unity. This project is a simple RPG where the objective is to reconstruct a ship to leave the planet we crashed on. The project includes basic combat with dice rolls, walking around and picking up objects.

project10.title: Approximation of physical processes for the artistic modeling of terrains
project10.subtitle: 3D R&D project
project10.description: A two person university project, the idea was to choose a 3D topic, do some research and implementing our findings using C++ and OpenGL, in other words this was a relatively free R&D project. As both of us are heavily passionate about video games and terrain generations and simulations, a real time approximation of physical processes of a terrain was one we really wanted to do. Our terrains are composed of 4 material layers (Bedrock, Stone, Sand and Water), 4 layers we call feature layers (layer elevation to converge to, water drain/water source). Our UI allows us to draw on these heightmaps to allow for more artistic liberty of the the terrain, and a choice of 6 physical approximations to choose from to modify the terrain over time (Thermal erosion, hydraulic erosion using shallow water simulation, rain, particle based wind with sediment transport, sandstorm, cimentation

project11.title: MAIge Academy VR
project11.subtitle: A Godot VR game
project11.description: Delve into a magical experience in your first day at MAIge Academy VR. Where you are taught many a spells with multiple casting techniques in order to solve various puzzles. This video game was developed in a group of 4, with a major focus on innovative use of the VR medium, as well as strong immersion while avoiding the discomfort that comes with the platform. We proposed multiple casting types (Voice command, drawing on surfaces with shape detection, casting spells using spell orbs) with many spells for each.

project12.title: Univ'hérbe cité
project12.subtitle: Godot 3D video game
project12.description: A serious game that has the player explore a fictional scenario all while learning about the interesting plants that grow on our university campus. There is a bonus for new students as it allows them to explore a somewhat accurate model of the university. This project was done in a group of 4, and aims to merge the gameplay and learning loops, creating puzzles that require you to learn about plants to be solvable.

project13.title: Age filter : creation of a neural network
project13.subtitle: An AI research project
project13.description: This project was centered around researching neural networks and apllying what we could find to create an aging filter. It involved implementing VAEs which we thoroughly pushed through trial and error to find our most convincing results, creating an adverserial network (GAN) using our VAE as the basis, and then researching powerful GANs, in our case StyleGAN, and fine tuning the model to more accurately work on our own databases.

job1.title: Tools & Pipeline Developer Apprenticeship
job1.subtitle: Illogic Studios
job1.description:
The apprenticeship during the final year of my masters degree (Sept 2025 - Aug 2026)
. My main task was to implement, fix, and refactor tools to aid artists, or the production team.
 This meant quick, smaller scale and varied tasks, it taught me how to quickly adapt to new APIs, languages and ways of thinking having worked on many softwares (Houdini, Prism, Deadline, Nuke, Maya, etc.) for many different tasks (.rat file manager, distant machine render, auto-publishing tools, auto Slap tools, etc.). As the company was growing, a need for a more robust developer pipeline was important, and aiding in its implementation also became an important part of my tasks. I was tasked with researching practices and discussing them, implementing gits, renewing them, publishing them as open source, cleaning code and documentation, as well as adopting coding conventions (Domain Driven Development, commit naming conventions, etc.)
